variants.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: ONE COMPLETE transparent square PNG game-item state, not a sprite sheet.
Input image 1 is the exact identity, paint style, camera, material, dimensions and proportions master: the accepted repaired C state of the Loststar mechanical date stamp. Input image 2 is ONLY a guide to which faults remain in state B; do not adopt its smoother rendering or elongated handle.
Primary request: edit image 1 into state B, CLEANED BUT NOT MECHANICALLY REPAIRED. Preserve image 1's broad flattened purple bulb, short narrowed neck and collar, short copper shaft, same brass housing silhouette and wall thickness, three original rollers and abstract purple bar marks. Keep the same three-quarter viewpoint, warm upper-left lighting, dark-purple edges, restrained broken golden highlights and fine but visibly pixel-painted clusters. Same scale and framing. Do not make a new smoother 3D model or add dense photorealistic microtexture.
Only mechanical differences from image 1: the entire purple handle and its attached shaft lean left about 10 degrees around the existing housing socket (the bulb itself must remain the SAME shape and relative size, merely tilted), the middle roller sits slightly lower and crooked, and the existing front-right round screw is slightly loose in its own hole. All parts remain physically attached. Keep the master housing EXACTLY where it was; no perspective change, no enlarged front mouth, no elongated bulb, no new seams or mechanisms.
Clean surfaces but preserve ALL master paint chips, old wood wear, brass edge scuffs and age. Cleaning does not repaint, replace missing varnish, polish to a mirror, straighten the shaft or align the rollers. No green oxidation or encrusted ink in this B state.
Output a coherent full object, one authored image. Genuine transparent alpha background; preserve transparent margins. No floor, cast shadow plane, cabinet, glass, tools, hands, text, labels, aura, particles, new lights or floating pieces. Not a collage, not copied chunks, no cut-paper patchwork.
